## Summary

Extreme Networks is a US maker of wired and wireless network infrastructure, founded in California in 1996, headquartered in Morrisville, North Carolina, and publicly traded on Nasdaq as EXTR [1]. The IEEE registry lists 94 MA-L blocks to "Extreme Networks, Inc.", almost all at its Morrisville address [2]. It grew by acquisition: Enterasys in 2013, Zebra Technologies' wireless LAN business in 2016, Avaya's networking business and Brocade's switching, routing and analytics business in 2017, and Aerohive in 2019 [1]; Aerohive had shipped its first 802.11ax access points in 2018 [3]. A MAC in an Extreme block is most likely an enterprise switch, router or access point, in a campus, branch or data-center network rather than a home.

Its products are sold as ExtremeSwitching, ExtremeRouting, ExtremeWireless, ExtremeXOS and ExtremeCloud IQ [1]. The radios and silicon in Extreme's own access points, FCC grantee codes, address randomization and security advisories are not documented by the sources consulted: Extreme's datasheet and advisory pages and the FCC ID databases were not reachable from this session, and nothing is filled in from memory.
